correctness.rationale: The incidence graph between two- and three-subsets realizes the double cover by complementing the negative side. At a landmark, sign parity distinguishes opposite sides, while within a side the three distance classes 0,1,2 of Petersen projections map injectively to the lifted distances. Thus resolving is equivalent to resolving the projection; two distinct projected landmarks have collisions in both intersecting and disjoint cases. On five points three distinct edges have only the star, triangle, path and path-plus-edge types. The listed collision pairs exclude every nonstar type, and all seven off-landmark signatures of the star are distinct. Unique centers are preserved by a single exchange because the shared pair of distinct spokes fixes the center. Within a center, replace the differing spoke if necessary, then fix mismatched signs; each move adds exactly one shared signed vertex, proving distance 3-|S∩T| and connectivity. The shell counts follow by fixing the omitted spoke (sign choices) or changing it (three choices of newly omitted spoke, two signs on the formerly absent spoke). Independent incidence-graph Floyd–Warshall and pair-separation-mask replay verified the GP(10,3) isomorphism, the lift distance table, all 190 pairs and 1140 triples, the exact 160 bases, and every exchange distance including disconnection. It gave five 32-vertex components, degree 9, 720 total edges and shells 1,9,15,7 at every basis.
residual_risks: The findings concern vertex metric bases of this graph and unconstrained single-landmark replacements within the bases, not redundant resolving sets or other reconfiguration moves.

value.rationale: A scalar dimension or failure of one exchange leaves open whether optimal landmarks can be repositioned without ever using more of them. For a canonical bipartite cover, the proof answers that question exactly: the projected star center is the persistent obstruction, while within each center the metric attains the obvious overlap lower bound. This makes the classified state space useful beyond its raw size.
residual_risks: No assertion that other double covers or generalized Petersen graphs share the exchange structure.
